verses.text: Then Darius the king made a decree, and the house of the archives, where the treasures were laid up in Babylon, was searched.
A scroll was found at Achmetha, in the palace that is in the province of Media, and in it this was written for a record:

In the first year of Cyrus the king, Cyrus the king made a decree: Concerning God’s house at Jerusalem, let the house be built, the place where they offer sacrifices, and let its foundations be strongly laid; with its height sixty cubits,  and its width sixty cubits;
with three courses of great stones and a course of new timber. Let the expenses be given out of the king’s house.

Also let the gold and silver vessels of God’s house, which Nebuchadnezzar took out of the temple which is at Jerusalem, and brought to Babylon, be restored and brought again to the temple which is at Jerusalem, everything to its place. You shall put them in God’s house.
Now therefore, Tattenai, governor beyond the River, Shetharbozenai, and your companions the Apharsachites, who are beyond the River, you must stay far from there.
Leave the work of this house of God alone; let the governor of the Jews and the elders of the Jews build this house of God in its place.

Moreover I make a decree what you shall do for these elders of the Jews for the building of this house of God: that of the king’s goods, even of the tribute beyond the River, expenses must be given with all diligence to these men, that they not be hindered.

That which they have need of, including young bulls, rams, and lambs, for burnt offerings to the God of heaven; also wheat, salt, wine, and oil, according to the word of the priests who are at Jerusalem, let it be given them day by day without fail;
that they may offer sacrifices of pleasant aroma to the God of heaven, and pray for the life of the king, and of his sons.
I have also made a decree that whoever alters this message, let a beam be pulled out from his house, and let him be lifted up and fastened on it; and let his house be made a dunghill for this.

May the God who has caused his name to dwell there overthrow all kings and peoples who stretch out their hand to alter the same, to destroy this house of God which is at Jerusalem. I Darius have made a decree. Let it be done with all diligence.
Then Tattenai, the governor beyond the River, Shetharbozenai, and their companions did accordingly with all diligence, because Darius the king had sent a decree.

The elders of the Jews built and prospered, through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo. They built and finished it, according to the commandment of the God of Israel, and according to the decree of Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes king of Persia.
This house was finished on the third day of the month Adar, which was in the sixth year of the reign of Darius the king.
The children of Israel, the priests, the Levites, and the rest of the children of the captivity, kept the dedication of this house of God with joy.

They offered at the dedication of this house of God one hundred bulls, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs; and for a sin offering for all Israel, twelve male goats, according to the number of the tribes of Israel.
They set the priests in their divisions, and the Levites in their courses, for the service of God, which is at Jerusalem, as it is written in the book of Moses.
The children of the captivity kept the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.

Because the priests and the Levites had purified themselves together, all of them were pure. They killed the Passover for all the children of the captivity, for their brothers the priests, and for themselves.
The children of Israel who had returned out of the captivity, and all who had separated themselves to them from the filthiness of the nations of the land, to seek Yahweh, the God of Israel, ate,

and kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with joy; because Yahweh had made them joyful, and had turned the heart of the king of Assyria to them, to strengthen their hands in the work of God, the God of Israel’s house.

footnotes.content: King Darius searches the archives—and what a patient God we have, who moves even pagan rulers to do His will. The work that was blocked finds an unexpected door.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A scroll found at Achmetha, in Media's palace—history preserved, waiting. The Lord's word written down outlasts every obstacle.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Cyrus's own decree confirms what his heart once turned to do. The temple to be built sixty cubits in height and width—a space where heaven and earth can meet again.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Great stones, new timber, king's treasury—God had been preparing all this before the first brick was asked for. Even the materials were ready when faith moved forward.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The vessels taken in captivity—gold and silver from the temple of God—must be restored. What was broken is being healed, piece by piece, vessel by vessel.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Darius speaks directly to the governors who once stood in the way. His authority turns the tide—sometimes the Lord silences opposition through a word of kingly power.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Let the Jews build their God's house in its place. Permission granted—not just tolerated, but the king's own command protects them now.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The king's goods shall fund this work—not a pittance, but diligence and treasure given so the building will not be hindered. The Lord provides through places we do not expect.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bulls, rams, lambs, wheat, salt, wine, oil—given daily without fail. The Lord sees the smallest need and holds the king's heart to meet it, day after day.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sacrifices rise in pleasant aroma; prayers asked for the king's life and his sons. Even in restoration, the people remember to intercede for those who serve the work.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Alter the decree? Your house becomes a dunghill, your body a warning. The king stakes his own reputation on protecting God's work—an iron promise.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The God who dwells in that house shall overthrow kings and peoples who lift a hand against it. When God claims a place for His name, He guards it with authority that transcends earthly crowns.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Tattenai and Shetharbozenai, once obstacles, now move with all diligence. The decree from the king had transformed resistance into cooperation—they obeyed.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Haggai and Zechariah prophesied; the elders built and prospered. Three kings' decrees converged—Cyrus, Darius, Artaxerxes—yet the builders followed the God of Israel first.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Finished on the third of Adar, in Darius's sixth year. Seventy years after its burning, the temple rises again—God's timing is patient, but never late.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Children of Israel, priests, Levites, all the captives kept the dedication with joy. After anguish, here at last is the feast they had dreamed of together.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: One hundred bulls, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs, twelve goats—an abundance of gratitude, one for each tribe. Their offering said what words could not.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Priests and Levites set in their divisions, in their courses, as written in Moses' book. Order restored—the worship of God resumed in right order, as He commanded.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Passover kept on the fourteenth day of the first month—they remembered, as their fathers had remembered, God's ancient deliverance from Egypt.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Priests and Levites purified themselves, all of them pure together. Before feast, before sacrifice, came cleansing—the heart prepared for God's house.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Those who had separated themselves from the nations' filthiness, seeking Yahweh—grace drawn the faithful closer. To seek Him is to be counted among His.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo: the Lord still turns hearts toward His work, still gives joy where there had been captivity, still strengthens hands in service. As of 2026-10, we too have seen Him turn the heart of the powerful.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
